weeks.title: Course Overview, the 2026 FM Landscape, and AI-Native Engineering
weeks.goal: Understand what you will build (a small foundation model, released publicly), set up the full toolchain, and self-select honestly.
weeks.title_ko: 과목 소개, 2026 FM 지형도, 그리고 AI-Native 엔지니어링
weeks.goal_ko: 이번 학기에 만들 것(공개 배포하는 작은 foundation model)을 이해하고, 전체 toolchain을 설정하며, 수강 적합성을 스스로 솔직하게 판단합니다.

concept.topic: What this course produces: walk through OlmoEarth-Nano (1.4M params) and Presto (~400K) as proof that real EO pretraining fits Colab-scale compute; show the capstone endpoint (HF Hub release + model card + eval table).

The 2026 landscape in one pass: three generations of geospatial FMs (MAE-era → sensor-agnostic multimodal → global embedding fields like AlphaEarth/TESSERA); ML weather is operational (ECMWF AIFS since Feb 2025, NOAA AIGFS Jan 2026, Google WeatherNext 2) — the frontier is now probabilistic skill, obs-direct pipelines, and honest evaluation.

AI-agent-native engineering: what Claude Code/Cursor are good at (scaffolding, refactors, sweeps) and bad at (silent numerical bugs, eval leakage); the verification discipline — you own every number; repo hygiene, commit-per-lab, research notes as first-class output.

Logistics + honest self-selection: grading (10/30/60), site sign-in (id = student number), lead-pair sign-up. Explicit statement: "the two papers assigned today are due as tickets before Week 2 — if they take you more than ~6 hours and still feel opaque, this course will feel like that every week."

Assigning the Week 1 readings in class: a guided walkthrough of Attention Is All You Need + ViT — what to look for, how to read them; both tickets (W1+W2) due Sun 9/6 13:00 on this site. First journal club is W2, instructor-moderated.
Preview of W2 and lab kickoff.

lab.task: (a) Environment: Python + PyTorch on Colab and/or the shared GPU server, uv/conda, GPU sanity check. (b) Create personal course repo with GitHub Pages (Quarto or MkDocs-Material) and publish Research Note 01. (c) With the agent, build and train a small CNN classifier on EuroSAT (RGB), ~10 epochs, and manually verify one gradient with a finite-difference check the agent writes tests for.
lab.deliverable: Live course-site account activated (password changed), environment verified, first CNN trained; Research Note 01 drafted in the repo — PDF submitted on this site by Sun 9/6 23:59 as part of HW0.

primary.title: Vaswani et al. 2017 — Attention Is All You Need
Dosovitskiy et al. 2020 — An Image is Worth 16x16 Words (ViT)

optional.title: He et al. 2021 — Masked Autoencoders (MAE), skim; returns in W7

questions: Why does attention scale as O(n²) in tokens, and what does that imply for a 0.25° global weather grid (721×1440)?
ViT needs more data than CNNs to win — what inductive biases were traded away, and do satellite images restore any of them?
What exactly is a 'token' for a multispectral image cube?

weeks.title: Leakage-Safe Evaluation Design (and the Fundamentals Recap)
weeks.goal: Design evaluations that survive spatial/temporal autocorrelation — the geoscience failure mode — with the optimization recipe compressed to a working recap.
weeks.title_ko: Leakage 없는 평가 설계 (그리고 기초 복습)
weeks.goal_ko: 지구과학의 대표적 실패 요인인 공간·시간 자기상관을 견디는 평가를 설계하고, optimization 레시피를 실전용 복습으로 압축합니다.

concept.topic: Backprop as vector–Jacobian products; where activation memory goes (sets up gradient checkpointing in W12) — compressed recap, full derivation in the handout
The optimizer recipe every FM in this course uses: AdamW, LR warmup + cosine schedule, weight decay vs L2, gradient clipping; regularization and early stopping in one pass

HEADLINE — leakage in environmental data: spatial and temporal autocorrelation, why random splits lie, effective sample size under blocked CV; spatial-block and temporal-holdout design; train/test year separation as WeatherBench2 does it
Designing a split a reviewer cannot reject: worked example on a global soil-moisture model (holdout by region, by year, by station network)

lab.task: Predict runoff ratio and mean annual streamflow from CAMELS-US catchment attributes (~671 basins, tabular). Agent builds MLP + gradient-boosting baseline; W&B sweep (LR, depth, dropout); then re-evaluate with spatial-block CV (holdout by HUC region) and quantify the optimism gap vs random splits.
lab.deliverable: Note 02 with sweep parallel-coordinates plot + a 'random split vs spatial split' table; one-paragraph leakage post-mortem.

primary.title: Reichstein et al. 2019 — Deep learning and process understanding for data-driven Earth system science (Nature)

optional.title: Schultz et al. 2021 — Can deep learning beat NWP?

questions: Which of Reichstein's five challenges have FMs since addressed, and which have they dodged?
Design a split for a global soil-moisture model that a reviewer couldn't reject — what do you hold out?
Is 'hybrid physics-ML' (their vision) winning in 2026, given NeuralGCM vs pure-ML GraphCast?

book.title: Goodfellow, Deep Learning — Ch. 6 (Deep Feedforward Networks, §6.1–6.5) + Ch. 8 (Optimization, §8.1–8.5)

weeks.title: Environmental Big Data and Cloud-Native Pipelines
weeks.goal: Fluently move satellite, reanalysis, and in-situ data through cloud-native formats; meet ERA5 and cos-latitude weighting.
weeks.goal_ko: 위성·재분석·현장 관측 데이터를 cloud-native 포맷으로 자유롭게 다루고, ERA5와 cos-latitude 가중을 처음 만납니다.

concept.topic: The data zoo: SMAP L3/L4, ERA5/MERRA-2 (reanalysis ≠ observation ≠ analysis), MODIS, GPM IMERG, HLS, Sentinel-1/2; spatial/temporal resolutions, latencies, error characteristics.
Cloud-native geospatial: COG, Zarr, STAC, chunking and why it dominates throughput; NASA Earthdata/earthaccess, Copernicus Data Space, Google/AWS public buckets, WeatherBench2's public ERA5 Zarr.

ERA5 as a pretraining corpus: equiangular grids, pressure levels, why area weighting exists — derive the cos-lat weighted mean; anomalies vs climatology (sets up ACC in W11); regridding: conservative vs bilinear remapping and when each is correct.
Designing dataset objects for pretraining: chips, tiles, per-pixel time series; normalization statistics done right (per-band, train-set-only).
Lab briefing: what the agent will scaffold vs what you must verify.

lab.task: Agent-built ETL, two pipes: (a) open WeatherBench2's public ERA5 Zarr (5.625° subset) with xarray, compute a Z500 climatology and anomaly field, verify a cos-lat weighted global mean of T2m against a naive mean; (b) pull ~200 Sentinel-2 L2A chips (64×64, 4 bands) over South Korea via STAC (Earth Search on AWS) or HLS via earthaccess, with SCL-based cloud/QA filtering applied when selecting chips, and write a local Zarr/NPZ chip store with per-band stats.
lab.deliverable: Reusable data/ module + Note 03 (chip gallery, anomaly map, weighted-vs-naive mean table). This chip store is reused in W7.

primary.title: Rolf et al. 2024 — Position: Satellite data is a distinct modality in ML

optional.title: Bauer, Thorpe & Brunet 2015 — The quiet revolution of NWP (Nature)

questions: Which of Rolf's claimed distinctions actually change architecture choices (cite SatMAE/Scale-MAE design decisions)?
Reanalysis is a model product — what does that mean for 'ground truth' when we evaluate a weather FM against ERA5?
Why is chunking layout a scientific issue, not just an engineering one?

book.title: Goodfellow, Deep Learning — Ch. 5 (Machine Learning Basics, §5.1–5.5)

weeks.title: CNNs and Spatiotemporal Modeling on Gridded Data
weeks.goal: Master the convolutional toolbox and dense-prediction craft that every FM is benchmarked against.
weeks.goal_ko: 모든 FM의 비교 기준이 되는 convolution 도구상자와 dense prediction 기법을 익힙니다.

concept.topic: Convolutions, receptive fields, encoder–decoder U-Net; skip connections as multi-scale fusion.
Dense prediction craft: segmentation losses (CE, Dice, focal), class imbalance, boundary effects, tiling/overlap inference.
Spatiotemporal extensions: ConvLSTM, 3D conv, factorized space–time; when convolution beats attention (small data, strong locality).
The humbling PANGAEA preview: well-tuned supervised U-Nets still beat many GFMs on many tasks — your capstone baselines must include one.
Multispectral input handling: >3 channels, per-band normalization, band dropout as augmentation.

lab.task: Flood extent segmentation on a Sen1Floods11 subset (~200 hand-labeled Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 chips, via TorchGeo). Agent scaffolds U-Net (segmentation-models-pytorch); student defines the eval (IoU, precision/recall, spatially disjoint split) and runs an ablation: S1-only vs S2-only vs fused input.
lab.deliverable: Note 04 with IoU table (3 input configs vs 'always-dry' baseline) + 4 prediction panels. This U-Net becomes the standing supervised baseline for capstone comparisons.

optional.title: Shi et al. 2015 — ConvLSTM for precipitation nowcasting

questions: Exactly what information do skip connections carry that the bottleneck destroys, and why does that matter more at 10 m GSD than on ImageNet?
Where should a pretrained FM plug into a U-Net-style decoder (this is what TerraTorch/Prithvi do)?
Why did ConvLSTM lose to transformers for global weather but survive for nowcasting (MetNet-3)?

weeks.title: Sequence Models, Autoregressive Forecasting, and Rollout Stability
weeks.goal: LSTMs for hydrologic time series, and the autoregressive rollout mechanics that all ML weather models live or die by.
weeks.title_ko: 시퀀스 모델, Autoregressive 예측, Rollout 안정성
weeks.goal_ko: 수문 시계열을 위한 LSTM과, 모든 ML 기상 모델의 성패를 가르는 autoregressive rollout 메커니즘을 배웁니다.

concept.topic: RNN/LSTM/GRU mechanics; gradients through time; why LSTMs still rule rainfall–runoff (the CAMELS story, NSE/KGE metrics).

Autoregressive forecasting as a discipline: teacher forcing vs free-running, exposure bias, error accumulation, multi-step (rollout) training curricula — exactly GraphCast's 1→12-step curriculum and Pangu's hierarchical 1/3/6/24-h models, previewed on 1-D problems.
Stability and blurring: why MSE-trained autoregressive models regress to the mean at long lead times; first look at the double-penalty problem.
Probabilistic outputs on time series: quantile loss, NLL heads — CRPS foreshadowed.
Lab briefing.

lab.task: Train an LSTM on CAMELS-US forcing→streamflow for ~30 basins (NeuralHydrology or plain PyTorch). Key experiment: compare 1-step-ahead teacher-forced skill vs free-running 15-day rollout; plot NSE vs lead time; add a 3-step rollout loss and show the stability gain. Close with a 20-min ERA5 teaser: single-variable next-step prediction on the WeatherBench2 5.625° Zarr — the weather-direction seed.
lab.deliverable: Note 05 with NSE-vs-lead-time curves for both training regimes + hydrograph panels + the ERA5 next-step teaser result.

primary.title: Kratzert et al. 2019 — Towards learning universal, regional, and local hydrological behaviors (HESS)

optional.title: Nearing et al. 2024 — Global prediction of extreme floods in ungauged watersheds (Nature)

questions: Map Kratzert's 'regional model + static attributes' onto FM vocabulary: what is pretraining, what is conditioning?
Derive why 1-step MSE training produces unstable long rollouts; what are three remedies (curriculum, multi-step loss, noise injection)?
Is streamflow prediction in ungauged basins a 'fine-tuning' or 'zero-shot' problem?

weeks.title: Attention and the Transformer, Built From Scratch (With an Agent You Verify)
weeks.goal: Own every line of a Transformer/ViT implementation; understand the positional-encoding choices EO and weather models hinge on.
weeks.title_ko: Attention과 Transformer, 밑바닥부터 구현 (에이전트와 함께, 직접 검증)
weeks.goal_ko: Transformer/ViT 구현의 모든 줄을 직접 책임지고, EO·기상 모델의 핵심인 positional encoding 선택을 이해합니다.

concept.topic: Attention from first principles: QKV, multi-head, masking, complexity; pre-norm vs post-norm; residual stream intuition.

Positional encodings as the geoscience battleground: sincos, learned, RoPE (one slide); then the ones that matter here — SatMAE's temporal+spectral encodings, Prithvi-EO-2.0's lat/lon+date embeddings, Scale-MAE's GSD encoding, ClimaX's variable tokenization.
ViT anatomy: patchify as tokenization; patch size vs sequence length vs resolution trade-offs (why weather models at 0.25° need tricks).
Windowed/shifted attention (Swin) and why Pangu, FuXi, and Aurora are Swin-based; 3D windows for pressure levels.
Mixed-precision and FlashAttention as "why your lab fits in 60 minutes."

lab.task: Implement mini_vit.py (attention, MHA, block, patchify, ViT) from scratch with the agent — test-driven: student specifies shape tests, causal-mask tests, a gradient-flow test, and an equivalence test against torch.nn.MultiheadAttention before the agent writes code. Train the tiny ViT (~1M params) on EuroSAT-MS (13-band Sentinel-2) with per-band-group patch embedding.
lab.deliverable: Note 06 + mini_vit.py with passing test suite committed; accuracy vs the W1 CNN. This file is the backbone of the W7 MAE and, for many students, the capstone.

questions: Why does shifted windowing recover cross-window information flow — and what is the weather-model analog at the poles/dateline?
For a 13-band image, argue for/against: one patch embed for all bands vs band-group embeds vs wavelength-conditioned embeds (DOFA's answer).
Presto has 400K params and competes with giants on pixel time series — what does that say about scale vs inductive fit?

book.title: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai) — Ch. 11 (Attention Mechanisms & Transformers)

weeks.title: Self-Supervised Learning: Pretrain Your First Model
weeks.goal: Understand the SSL design space and actually pretrain a mini-MAE on satellite imagery — everyone's hands-on pretraining experience and the capstone seed.
weeks.goal_ko: SSL 설계 공간을 이해하고 위성 영상으로 mini-MAE를 실제로 pretraining합니다 — 전원이 직접 해보는 pretraining 경험이자 capstone의 씨앗입니다.

concept.topic: SSL taxonomy with lineage map: masked reconstruction (MAE → SatMAE/Prithvi), contrastive (SimCLR), self-distillation (DINO → DINOv3-satellite), latent prediction (I-JEPA → Galileo, AnySat, OlmoEarth's Latent MIM Lite); collapse and how each family avoids it.
MAE mechanics in detail: 75% masking, asymmetric encoder/decoder, normalized-pixel targets, why high masking works for images and what changes for EO (spatial redundancy, cloud pixels).
Structured masking for EO/weather: spatial, spectral/band-group, temporal, and modality masking (SatMAE, SpectralGPT, Galileo); Prithvi-WxC's mixed masked+forecast objective as the bridge to W11.
Evaluating SSL: linear probe vs kNN vs full fine-tune; why probe rankings mislead (GEO-Bench-2 evidence).
Mixed precision (torch.amp) introduced hands-on in the lab today.

lab.task: In-class core: pretrain a mini-MAE (~2M params, from your W6 ViT) on the W3 Sentinel-2/HLS chip store (or a ~5k-chip SSL4EO-S12 subset), bf16 autocast, ~15 min on one GPU; then linear probe on EuroSAT vs (a) random init and (b) supervised-from-scratch at equal epochs; visualize reconstructions.
lab.deliverable: Note 07 with probe-accuracy table (pretrained vs random vs supervised) and reconstruction grids. This checkpoint and codebase are every student's hands-on pretraining experience and the capstone seed — reused in the W9 scaling sweep and the W10 leaderboard; the HydroAI lab's Hydro-FM team builds on it directly.
lab.homework: Masking-ratio ablation: rerun pretraining at 50/75/90% masking; add reconstruction grids and the probe mini-ablation table to Note 07.

primary.title: He et al. 2021 — Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

questions: Why can MAE mask 75% while BERT masks 15% — and what ratio would you predict for cloud-free Sentinel-2 vs ERA5 fields (compare Prithvi-WxC's choice)?
What exactly does the decoder learn, and why throw it away?
Propose one EO-specific masking structure and the invariance it would induce.

weeks.title: Midterm: Portfolio Review and Capstone Proposal Pitches
weeks.goal: Convert seven weeks of labs into a credible, compute-budgeted capstone proposal.
weeks.title_ko: 중간 점검: 포트폴리오 리뷰와 Capstone 제안 발표
weeks.goal_ko: 지난 7주의 실습을 compute 예산까지 갖춘 설득력 있는 capstone 제안서로 완성합니다.

concept.topic: How to write a capstone proposal: data → objective → architecture → compute budget → evaluation-first design (name your baselines and metrics before training anything).
Compute budgeting at course scale: back-of-envelope FLOPs, tokens-seen, GPU-hours; Chinchilla logic previewed (formalized in W9).

Track briefing: default track for everyone = fine-tune and rigorously evaluate a public FM (LoRA, free-tier compute); pretraining is experienced by all in the W7/W9 labs; from-scratch development is reserved for the HydroAI lab team's joint Hydro-FM project. Weather-direction proposals are provisional, with a revision gate after W11. Scope ladders for EV4240 vs EN5425.
Proposal pitches, round 1: 5-min pitch + 3-min hostile-but-kind Q&A per student/team (instructor + one assigned peer discussant each).

lab.task: Pitches continue; every student files written feedback (GitHub issues) on two peers' proposals; instructor sign-off queue. Portfolio spot-check: instructor clones two random repos and re-runs a lab note live — a reproducibility culture moment.
lab.deliverable: 2-page proposal (data, objective, base model, compute budget, downstream tasks, eval protocol, risk plan) — PDF submitted on this site by Sun 11/1 13:00; pitched in class 11/2.

weeks.title: Foundation Models and Scaling Laws
weeks.goal: The intellectual frame — what makes a model a foundation model, and how scaling laws let you budget a tiny one honestly.
weeks.goal_ko: 무엇이 모델을 foundation model로 만드는지라는 지적 틀과, scaling law로 작은 모델의 예산을 정직하게 세우는 법을 다룹니다.

concept.topic: Foundation-model definition (Bommasani): emergence and homogenization; what transfers from the LLM playbook to EO/weather and what doesn't (no internet-scale text; data is spatially correlated and physically constrained).
Scaling laws: Kaplan power laws, Chinchilla compute-optimal N vs D, data-constrained scaling; worked example live: 'you have 10 GPU-hours and 50 GB of chips — solve for model size'.
When pretraining pays: transfer gap vs supervised baselines; PANGAEA/GEO-Bench-2 evidence that it often doesn't — framing your capstone claim honestly.
Emergence skepticism and evaluation-metric artifacts; what 'emergent' could even mean for a weather model.
Lab briefing: you will fit your own scaling law today.

lab.task: Fit a mini scaling law for your own model family. The 4-size sweep (launched pre-class as homework) is already done; the 60 in-class minutes go to fitting and diagnosing the power law: plot reconstruction loss (and probe accuracy) vs params on log–log, fit the power law, stress-test where the fit breaks, and extrapolate to your capstone budget — writing the prediction into your proposal.
lab.deliverable: Note 09 with the log–log fit reported as a prediction interval plus enumerated failure modes (not a point prediction) + a one-paragraph capstone budget memo (chosen N, D, GPU-hours, predicted loss range).
lab.homework: Pre-class: launch the 4-size scaling sweep (~0.1M/0.5M/2M/8M params, fixed wall-clock on the fixed chip corpus) so all runs finish before the lab.

primary.title: Hoffmann et al. 2022 — Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)

optional.title: Kaplan et al. 2020 — Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
Bommasani et al. 2021 — Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models (Secs. 1–2)

questions: Chinchilla says balance N and D — what is 'a token' of ERA5, and how many does 40 years of 0.25° reanalysis contain?
Why might scaling exponents differ for satellite imagery vs text?
Given your W9 lab fit: is your capstone compute-optimal, over-parameterized, or data-starved?

weeks.title: Earth Observation Foundation Models (EO-FM Week)
weeks.goal: Command the GFM design space — from SatMAE to embedding fields — and how to evaluate them without fooling yourself.
weeks.goal_ko: SatMAE부터 embedding field까지 GFM 설계 공간을 장악하고, 스스로를 속이지 않고 평가하는 법을 배웁니다.

concept.topic: Generation 1: SatMAE (temporal/spectral tokens, band-group masking), Scale-MAE (GSD positional encoding, Laplacian decoder), Prithvi-EO-1.0/2.0 (HLS, 3D geolocation+date embeddings, TerraTorch fine-tuning stack — the closest published blueprint to your capstone).

Generation 2, sensor-agnostic and multimodal: DOFA/Copernicus-FM (wavelength-conditioned hypernetwork patch embeds), TerraMind (any-to-any generation, Thinking-in-Modalities), Galileo (dual global+local latent objectives, structured space/time/modality masking), SpectralGPT, SkySense.

Generation 3, embeddings as the product: AlphaEarth Foundations (64-D annual 10 m embeddings in GEE — a 'virtual satellite', not a backbone), TESSERA (open competitor), Major-TOM embeddings; OlmoEarth as the fully open small-model + platform exemplar; DINOv3-satellite as the outsider that wins on high-res RGB.
Honest evaluation: GEO-Bench → GEO-Bench-2 capability groups ('no model dominates'), PANGAEA's U-Net reality check, the 89-GFM usability study; what your capstone eval must therefore include.
Lab briefing.

lab.task: Mini-GFM leaderboard, in-class core: linear-probe three frozen encoders — (a) your W7 mini-MAE, (b) OlmoEarth-Nano (HF checkpoint), (c) Presto — on ONE classification task with the same split: EuroSAT-MS.
lab.deliverable: Note 10 — leaderboard table + 200-word 'which encoder for which task and why', citing GEO-Bench-2's capability-group logic.
lab.homework: Optional extensions: a dense-task probe (Sen1Floods11 with a 1×1-conv head) and a fourth AlphaEarth Satellite Embeddings column from GEE over a Korean AOI. Required: capstone corpus curation — assemble and document your fine-tuning dataset (default track) or pretraining chip corpus (Hydro-FM team).

questions: Which Prithvi-EO-2.0 design choices survive at 1/1000th scale, and which are pointless below 100M params?
Are location/date embeddings a feature or a leakage channel for downstream tasks?
If AlphaEarth-style embedding fields keep improving, who still needs to fine-tune a backbone — and what does that mean for your capstone's claim?

weeks.title: Weather and Climate Foundation Models (Weather-FM Week)
weeks.goal: The full ML-weather stack: paradigms, spherical geometry, rollout stability, and WeatherBench2-grade evaluation — then train your own tiny forecaster.
weeks.goal_ko: ML 기상의 전체 스택 — 패러다임, 구면 기하, rollout 안정성, WeatherBench2급 평가 — 을 다룬 뒤, 직접 작은 forecaster를 학습합니다.

concept.topic: Problem setup: atmospheric state as a tensor (variables × levels × lat × lon), ERA5 as corpus, initial-condition provenance (ERA5 vs operational analysis — an evaluation trap), 2026 operational status (AIFS, NOAA AIGFS, WeatherNext 2).

Paradigm tour, one architecture slide each: deterministic transformers (Pangu's 3D Earth-specific attention, Stormer, FuXi/FengWu), graph/mesh (GraphCast's icosahedral encode-process-decode, AIFS), spherical operators (SFNO — why FFTs on lat-lon grids are wrong at the poles), probabilistic/generative (GenCast diffusion, FGN/WeatherNext 2, FourCastNet 3), hybrid (NeuralGCM), obs-direct (Aardvark, GraphDOP), and the pretrain→fine-tune FMs proper (ClimaX variable tokenization, Aurora, Prithvi-WxC).
Rollout stability engineering: multi-step loss curricula (GraphCast's schedule), fine-tuning horizon, blurring/double-penalty, power-spectra diagnostics, effective resolution.

Metrics you must be able to derive: lat-weighted RMSE, ACC vs climatology (and the 0.6 'useful skill' convention), bias; probabilistic: CRPS as generalized MAE, spread–skill, rank histograms; the WeatherBench2 protocol (test years, headline scorecard).

lab.task: Train a tiny weather emulator on the WeatherBench2 ERA5 5.625° Zarr (Z500 + T850, 6-h steps, ~1979–2015 train / 2018–2019 test): small U-Net or your W6 ViT (~1–3M params) predicting residual (Δstate) targets, with per-variable-per-level normalization and static input channels (orography, land–sea mask). Write the lat-weighted MSE loss yourself and test it against analytic values (agent writes the test). Evaluate lat-weighted RMSE and ACC vs persistence and climatology baselines at 1–5-day leads via autoregressive rollout; plot the zonal power spectrum at day 1 vs day 5 to see blurring.
lab.deliverable: Note 11 — WB2-style scorecard table (model vs persistence vs climatology), ACC-vs-lead-time plot, spectra figure, rollout animation GIF. This is the weather-direction capstone seed; provisional W8 weather proposals hit their revision gate after this week.

questions: Derive why unweighted MSE on a lat-lon grid over-weights the poles, and by how much at 60°N.
GraphCast beats HRES on RMSE partly by blurring — how would CRPS-trained GenCast change that comparison, and what does the double-penalty argument say?
Is an ERA5 emulator forecasting the atmosphere or forecasting ECMWF's data assimilation system? Defend both readings.

weeks.title: Scaling the Pipeline: Training Engineering, Fine-Tuning, and Release
weeks.goal: Every remaining capstone skill: efficient training at your compute ceiling, PEFT fine-tuning, ablation design, and a real HF Hub release — after this week you have 100% of the capstone skill set.
weeks.title_ko: 파이프라인 확장: Training 엔지니어링, Fine-Tuning, 릴리스
weeks.goal_ko: capstone에 필요한 나머지 기술 전부 — compute 한도 내 효율적 학습, PEFT fine-tuning, ablation 설계, 실제 HF Hub 릴리스 — 를 익혀 이번 주로 capstone 기술 세트를 100% 갖춥니다.

concept.topic: Training engineering: bf16/AMP recap, gradient accumulation, activation/gradient checkpointing (memory math from W2 revisited), DDP concepts (all-reduce, effective batch size, LR scaling) and when FSDP matters; streaming dataloaders (WebDataset/streaming Zarr) so GPUs never starve.

Fine-tuning spectrum: linear probe → decoder-only → LoRA/PEFT (derive the low-rank update, rank/alpha choices) → full FT; decoder heads for dense EO tasks (UperNet-style, TerraTorch conventions) and forecast heads for weather.

Evaluation and ablation design for the capstone: minimum honest set = {random-init control, supervised baseline (your W4 U-Net or persistence/climatology), frozen probe, fine-tuned}, one ablation axis (masking ratio, data volume, or model size), seeds and error bars.
Significance testing for forecast and benchmark comparisons: paired block bootstrap over time (and space), why naive per-sample tests lie under autocorrelation, error bars for scorecard tables.

Release engineering: HF Hub mechanics (weights, config, README.md model card), semantic versioning, licenses for models and data (Copernicus, NASA open-data terms), W&B reports as the lab notebook of record.

lab.task: Capstone dress rehearsal, in-class core: (a) attach LoRA adapters (peft) to your W7/W9 pretrained mini-MAE (or OlmoEarth-Nano) and fine-tune on Sen1Floods11 (geo rehearsal) or fine-tune the W11 emulator on a Korea-region T2m patch (weather rehearsal); (b) build a CRPS mini-ensemble via MC-dropout and score it; (c) push the checkpoint to HF Hub with an agent-drafted, human-corrected model card; run DDP on 2 GPUs on the shared server if available (otherwise simulate with accumulation).
data: WeatherBench2 ERA5 Korea-region T2m patch (weather rehearsal)
lab.deliverable: Note 12 — LoRA fine-tune result, CRPS mini-ensemble score, live HF Hub link with model card; homework adds the three-way fine-tuning table and memory/throughput mini-benchmark.
lab.homework: Probe vs LoRA vs full-FT three-way comparison in one W&B report; enable gradient checkpointing + accumulation and measure the memory/throughput trade-off.

questions: Why can rank-8 updates match full fine-tuning — what does that imply about the geometry of task adaptation?
For a 2M-param model, is PEFT ever worth it, or is it purely a big-model technology? Test your answer in the lab.
PANGAEA shows GFMs losing to U-Nets — list three experimental-design choices that could flip such a comparison dishonestly.

weeks.title: Agentic ML Engineering + Capstone Sprint 1
weeks.goal: Turn your AI agent from code generator into experiment orchestrator; launch the capstone run. Milestone M1 due.
weeks.goal_ko: AI 에이전트를 코드 생성기에서 실험 orchestrator로 격상시키고, capstone 학습 run을 시작합니다. Milestone M1 제출.

concept.topic: Agentic engineering for ML: multi-agent patterns (planner/implementer/reviewer), MCP servers for W&B and HF, agent-run ablation loops with guardrails (immutable eval script, human-approved config diffs).
CI for research code: smoke-test on 1 batch, deterministic seeds, config-as-code (hydra/yaml); pre-registration of the capstone eval protocol (frozen this week, before results exist).
Chinchilla applied: each team defends its N/D/GPU-hour triple against its W9 scaling fit in 60 seconds.

lab.task: Capstone sprint studio, led by Dr. Budamala: freeze data pipeline and eval protocol; launch fine-tuning/eval runs (checkpoint-resumable); design reviews at the bench. The instructor is at AGU — Dr. Budamala runs the session.
lab.deliverable: M1 (PDF on this site, due Fri 12/4 23:59): frozen data/ + eval/ modules with CI green; runs launched with public W&B link; pre-registered eval protocol.

questions: CRPS-trained GenCast redefines what a 'better' forecast means vs RMSE-optimized deterministic models — which metric should headline your capstone eval, and why?
Your data is capped — what does data-constrained (Chinchilla-with-epoching) scaling say about repeating epochs vs shrinking the model?
What can an agent safely automate in your capstone loop, and what must remain human-gated? Write the gate list into your repo.

weeks.title: Capstone Sprint 2 + Peer Code Review; Model Cards and Reproducibility
weeks.goal: Fine-tune and evaluate the model; subject your code to structured peer review. Milestone M2 due.
weeks.title_ko: Capstone Sprint 2 + 동료 코드 리뷰; Model Card와 재현성
weeks.goal_ko: 모델을 fine-tuning하고 평가하며, 코드를 구조화된 동료 리뷰에 부칩니다. Milestone M2 제출.

concept.topic: Model cards and data cards done properly: intended use, out-of-scope use, eval disaggregation (by region/biome/lead time), limitations that are specific, not liability boilerplate.
Reproducibility checklist: seeds, environment lockfiles, data versioning/DOIs, exact commit for every number in the report; license compatibility of your release.
Peer-review protocol: assigned reviewer pairs (geo↔weather cross-track), review = run their smoke test + read eval code + file ≥3 substantive GitHub issues.

lab.task: Capstone sprint studio, led by Dr. Budamala: downstream fine-tuning with the mandatory baseline set; structured peer code review in session (>=3 substantive issues given and received).
lab.deliverable: M2: checkpoint archived; ≥1 fine-tuned downstream result with baselines table; peer review given and received (issue links); draft model card in repo.

optional.title: Mitchell et al. 2019 — Model Cards for Model Reporting
How Usable Are Geospatial Foundation Models?

questions: Write the 'out-of-scope uses' section for your own model in three honest sentences.
Of the usability failures found across 89 GFMs, which three are cheapest to prevent — and does your repo prevent them?

weeks.title: Wrap-up: evaluation, documentation, release candidate — final polish week
weeks.goal: Finish evaluation and ablation, harden documentation, cut a release candidate. Milestone M3 due.
weeks.title_ko: 마무리: 평가·문서화·릴리스 후보 — 최종 정리 주간
weeks.goal_ko: 평가와 ablation을 마무리하고 문서를 다듬어 release candidate를 만듭니다. Milestone M3 제출.

concept.topic: Release engineering final pass: HF Hub versioned release, GitHub tag, W&B report as appendix, GitHub Pages project page.
Recorded-demo rubric: what the ~8-minute video must show (problem, data, evidence, baselines, ablation, limitations, live quickstart run).

lab.task: Final polish on your own schedule: complete the ablation, finalize eval tables with seeds/error bars, finish model card and README quickstart, tag the release candidate. Questions via GitHub issues.
lab.deliverable: M3: full results + ablation tables; complete model card; release candidate tagged on HF Hub + GitHub; draft slides.

questions: What would this paper's authors say is wrong with your capstone?
What is the smallest experiment that would extend your capstone toward this frontier?

weeks.title: Demo Week: recorded presentations + public release (no class meeting)
weeks.title_ko: 데모 주간: 녹화 발표 + 공개 릴리스 (수업 없음)

Release verification (async): an assigned peer + the instructor clone your repo fresh and run the README quickstart; it must work.
Course retrospective: what the 2026 landscape will look like in 2027; how to turn a capstone into a workshop paper (AGU/EGU, NeurIPS CCAI, ICLR ML4RS).
